summary: Hybrid prewarm sticker expiry causes silent downgrade to compatibility variant for some tenant traffic
description:
Issue summary:
A Streamline Analytics tenant observed a silent downgrade of a subset of production requests to the compatibility variant during a hybrid canary prewarm window. The requests had previously been servicing the pinned model (redwood/chat-medium-v2) but after an orchestrator prewarm step some sessions were routed to the compat model without customer-visible errors.

Impact:
- Customer reports increased token-level cost (~+28%) and a change in response style/quality for ~2.3% of requests across their us-west dedicated pool between 2026-03-12T18:03 and 2026-03-12T18:17.
- No 5xx errors surfaced; responses were valid but lower-quality. Customer latency SLOs remained met.

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 18:01:12 Prewarm wave initiated for canary fraction (hybrid prewarm: edge+serving prewarm).
- 18:03:04 Edge health probe rebalanced several prewarm connections.
- 18:03:27 We see a burst of orchestrator commit timeouts for sticker leases.
- 18:04:00 First customer report to support via portal.
- 18:06:45 Support triaged and escalated to SRE.
- 18:12:30 Temporary explicit model_pin applied by Support to affected tenant.
- 18:17:00 Traffic normalized, issue subsided.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dsp-usw-7 (NVIDIA A100), orchestrator v2.14.1, edge-proxy v1.9.
- Customer configured explicit model selection in route, but relies on platform sticky session behavior for long-lived sessions.

Steps to reproduce (investigative):
1) Start a controlled hybrid canary prewarm against a dedicated pool with the same tenant (use prewarm=hybrid flag).
2) Simulate a slow commit path by injecting 200-400ms latency on orchestrator commit RPCs.
3) Observe session sticker TTLs and orchestrator commit logs during the prewarm wave.

Observed behavior:
- Orchestrator logs show sticker-lease commit returned with "commit_timeout" for ~1.9% of handshakes.
- Edge routes those sessions to the compat-quant variant as a fallback path when the model_pin commit is not confirmed within the handshake window.
- No explicit pin-unset events were emitted; behavior appears as a silent downgrade rather than an explicit unpin.

Expected behavior:
- When a model_pin commit fails transiently during prewarm, requests should either retry the commit path or keep using the already-committed pin rather than steering to a lower-quality compat fallback without an explicit pin change.

Relevant logs / excerpts (sanitized):
- orchestrator[2026-03-12T18:03:27Z] commitSticker(tenant=streamline-42) -> timeout after 320ms, lease=sticker-0x7f3b
- edge[2026-03-12T18:03:31Z] routeDecision(tenant=streamline-42) -> fallbackRoute=compat-quant-v1 (reason=pin_commit_unconfirmed)
- serving[2026-03-12T18:04:10Z] modelSwitch(tenant=streamline-42) -> applied variant=compat-quant-v1 session=abcd1234

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support applied an explicit per-tenant model_pin via the admin API for streamline-42 at 18:12:30 which prevented further silent downgrades while engineering investigated.

Next steps and current mitigation:
- SRE/Eng to reproduce in staging with injected commit latency and confirm the commit-handshake code path.
- Patch orchestrator to extend sticker handshake TTL or allow edge to honor last-known committed pin until commit confirmation arrives.
- Add metric/alert for "pin_commit_unconfirmed" rate above 0.1% of handshakes for a tenant.
- Coordinate hotfix rollout (see related PR).

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: The prewarm path creates a short-lived 'sticker' lease to claim a session for a model variant during orchestration. If the orchestrator's commit RPC exceeds the handshake window (due to transient latency or backpressure), the edge chooses a fallback variant (compat-quant-v1) for safety. Because the last-known pin remains in control-plane state but the handshake was unconfirmed, we observed a silent downgrade instead of a transient retry or hold.
Data points: commit_timeout spikes align with cluster autoscaler activity at 18:02 and an internal control-plane GC at 18:03. A small subset of sessions did not receive commit confirmation before edge route decision.
Reproducer steps validated the condition in staging. No evidence of data corruption or incorrect pin metadata; this is ordering/timeout race.
Related: orchestration timeouts increased by ~4x for a 60s window during the prewarm wave. Edge routeDecision code currently treats unconfirmed commit as 'safe' to fallback quickly to compat rather than defer.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: Applied customer-scoped explicit model_pin via admin API to hold sessions on the desired variant (already performed).
Medium-term fix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3456): Increase sticker commit handshake TTL from 300ms to 800ms during hybrid prewarm; add a reconciliation path where edge will honor last-known committed pin for up to 5s if commit confirmation delayed.
Rollout plan: merge to v2.14.2-stable -> staged canary on staging -> prod canary in us-west only -> full rollout across dedicated pools. Expected risk low; change is TTL/handshake handling.
Postmortem action items:
- Instrument metric: pin_commit_unconfirmed_rate (per-tenant, per-region).
- Alert: >0.1% unconfirmed handshakes for any tenant for >5m -> auto-escalate to SRE.
- Update prewarm runbook to include jittered backoff on commit RPCs and a note to not aggressively fallback within first 5s of handshake.
- Customer follow-up: share explanation and ETA for fix; offer one week of usage credit to offset cost delta (coordinating with CS and Finance).
